Coffee drinkers of Voat, what's special about Turkish coffee?

The only experience I've had with is was when I went to a local Middle-Eastern restaurant. It was pretty good, but I would still prefer regular black coffee. It's probably an acquired taste though, similar to the previously mentioned regular black coffee.

It's strong. Very strong. Being Colombian the best comparison I can think is of Colombian strong coffee being served like an espresso.

Other than the obvious it comes with the fine grounds inside and what not, it's great. Whenever I have it I enjoy chewing on the fine grounds when they do get in the way.

http://www.mehmetefendi.com

These are THE guys. They have only one shop and distribute everywhere from that one shop. It is in the spice bazaar district of Istanbul. The people are queuing to get the freshest ground still hot from the grinders. The whole street smells unbelievable.

Turkish coffee is delicious. Thick, robust, and caffeinated. I chew the grounds. For me, it's part of the appeal. If a restaurant serves Turkish coffee, I will always order it. I don't make it at home because I'm likely to abuse it and then it will no longer be special .

I enjoyed it quite a bit, the grounds are so fine it is more like a powder mixed in to create a super strong kick in the tastebuds. From what I've been told, it's best to pair it with a croissant as the fine powder grounds stick to the pastry as you dip it. In fact, I was told that it was the origin of the crescent moon shaped pastry. An insult to the invading Turks by a cheeky baker.
I'm never going to check if this is true because this is the best possible origin story for croissants.
For an atheist who balks at superstition, I really enjoy seeing if I can make a prediction out of the shape of the grounds at the bottom of a cup.

Don't buy a grinder first up. See if you can find a middle eastern supermarket around somewhere near your house, as they will probably be able to sell you it ground already.

As for the special pot, don;t race out straight away, use a regular saucepan for a while, and then, if you are REALLY in to it, go and spend the money.

I need to generate a random range of integers between 1 and 2048 without repeating. I've found some ways online but none of them are efficient enough for me (I need to do this thousands of times). Anyone have any ideas?
[VBA] Need efficient way to produce random integers without repeating.
1 column of 1 to 2048 in order. Next column rand(). Select both columns. Sort by second column.

That worked great! Thanks! I can't believe I didn't think of this.

Edit: It turns out that to doing this in VBA, without printing to worksheet, isn't trivial...

Dim a(1 To 2048) As Integer
Dim i As Integer, swap As Integer, tmp As Integer

' Initialize a to (1 .. 2048)
For i=1 To 2048
 a(i)=i;
Next i

' shuffle a
For i=2048 To 2 Step -1
 swap = Int (Rnd * i) +1
 ' swap a(i) with a(swap)
 tmp = a(swap)
 a(swap) = a(i)
 a(i) = tmp
Next i

I've never actually used VBA, but the idea should be clear.
